answer: Each identity registers one voyage leg, locks an 80-credit bond and files a key-bound pulse log: leg serial, departure and arrival pulses, pearl seal. The auditor recomputes transit from the pulse-timing table (distance over speed) and checks the pearl seal on the registry; mismatch, reuse, or copying burns the bond. The first leg costs 36; the k-th 36+6(k-1); the 1,000th 6,030, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,033,000 fees plus 80,000 locked. A rented-pulse ring fails: each pulse binds to one leg and one epoch and is unreplayable. An honest agent pays 36 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
